qs.q:
Everybody Needs Good Neighbours — Which person…

A=Alice (old friends, known since school, leaves key with them, occasional problems — flooding, grateful for good neighbours)
B=Brian (pensioners next to students, considerate but sometimes too loud with stereo, respectful, could fix computer)
C=Conrad (previous neighbours fine, new ones made mess, pets, abused him when he complained, had nerve to ask for bike)
D=Doris (initially seemed decent, then dispute about fence/property, went to court, wish they had talked first)
E=Ella (heard horror stories but own experience great, neighbours' kids always round, shared birthday party, help fix things)
F=Francis (moved in, thought house next door was abandoned — so quiet, graffiti/broken window, discovered retired couple, never exchanged a word)

0. knew their neighbours before moving in? [A=Alice: 'we were at school together']
1. lives next door to people who no longer work?
2. does things together with the people next door?
3. sometimes lends their neighbours things?
4. lives next to people who can be noisy?
5. was surprised the first time they saw their neighbours?
6. has neighbours who keep animals?
7. lives next to people who once damaged their property?
8. says their problems with their neighbours were avoidable?
9. lives next to people who are very untidy?
10. says that the people next door are polite?
11. had legal problems with the neighbours?
12. lives next door to people who repair things for them?
items: 1 — lives next door to people who no longer work?
2 — does things together with the people next door?
4 — lives next to people who can be noisy?
5 — was surprised the first time they saw their neighbours?
7 — lives next to people who once damaged their property?
8 — says their problems with their neighbours were avoidable?
9 — lives next to people who are very untidy?
10 — says that the people next door are polite?
11 — had legal problems with the neighbours?
12 — lives next door to people who repair things for them?

qs.q:
Protest Punk

"We just thought that it would be A LAUGH TO TRY OURSELVES."

The author and his friends decided to start a band because…
A they liked the energy of the music they heard.
B they thought that they would have good fun.
C they wanted people to hear their political views.
D they were impressed by the image of punk.
opts: they liked the energy of the music they heard.
they thought that they would have good fun.
they wanted people to hear their political views.
they were impressed by the image of punk.

qs.q:
Protest Punk

"We wanted to send a message... that it DIDN'T MATTER WHO YOU WERE, because you could START A BAND TOO."

What does the author say about the band's music?
A It improved a lot as time passed.
B It showed anyone could be in a group.
C It was influenced by various styles.
D It was not as important as the words.
opts: It improved a lot as time passed.
It showed anyone could be in a group.
It was influenced by various styles.
It was not as important as the words.

qs.q:
Protest Punk

"The company WOULDN'T RELEASE IT. They said the politics were too risky. We weren't going to stand for CENSORSHIP, so we SET UP OUR OWN COMPANY."

Why did the band start their own record company?
A They wanted to help new groups record albums.
B They wanted to make records that were affordable.
C They wanted to sell more and reach more people.
D They wanted to sing about whatever they wished.
opts: They wanted to help new groups record albums.
They wanted to make records that were affordable.
They wanted to sell more and reach more people.
They wanted to sing about whatever they wished.

qs.q:
Protest Punk

"We knew they would TWIST AND DISTORT EVERYTHING WE SAID."

The band didn't do interviews with the media because…
A they believed journalists were not interested in the truth.
B they felt TV and newspapers were only interested in money.
C they wanted to avoid too much publicity about their lives.
D they wanted to promote smaller publications.
opts: they believed journalists were not interested in the truth.
they felt TV and newspapers were only interested in money.
they wanted to avoid too much publicity about their lives.
they wanted to promote smaller publications.

qs.q:
Protest Punk

"You can't RAISE KIDS when you're constantly touring."

Why did the group stop playing?
A To bring up their families.
B To give new bands a chance.
C To start a book company.
D To take a break from touring.
opts: To give new bands a chance.
To take a break from touring.

qs.q:
Protest Punk

"Before then, hardly anyone was a vegetarian and no one protested against injustice. Nowadays, there are MANY MORE PEOPLE LIKE THAT. We PLAYED A ROLE IN THAT."

What does the author think the band achieved?
A They contributed to improving animal rights.
B They had an effect on the music industry.
C They helped bring about changes in attitudes.
D They were a role model to young people.
opts: They contributed to improving animal rights.
They had an effect on the music industry.
They helped bring about changes in attitudes.
They were a role model to young people.

qs.q:
Learning Languages

"The 'verb table' looked like a mysterious mathematical formula and made just about as much sense. (19) ____. Teachers today tend to agree. Instead of using the old grammar/translation methods, they teach students how to achieve simple tasks."

A However, today's students are lucky to have a wide variety of multi-media programmes.
B As a result, beginners are more likely to learn how to buy a train ticket than how to form the plural.
C The best thing about learning in a small group is that it motivates you to use the language.
D The pronunciation of Portuguese was exhausting, Slovak consonants made my jaw ache.
E The best of them have quick exercises, photographs and real life recordings.
F Twelve years later I had a degree in French, but was convinced that there must be a better way.
G Indeed, the more languages you learn, the easier the process becomes.
H That is why, when I took up Spanish, I decided to go back into the communicative classroom.
opts: A — today's students are lucky to have multi-media programmes
B — beginners more likely to learn to buy a train ticket than form a plural
C — best thing about learning in small group
D — pronunciation of Portuguese was exhausting
E — best of them have quick exercises and real recordings
F — Twelve years later I had a degree in French, but convinced there must be a better way
G — the more languages you learn, the easier it becomes
H — that is why, when I took up Spanish, I went back to communicative classroom
